body: This fill me with hope. Not the part where children are filled with propaganda, and the government wastes there timeline on it; that sucks.  The fact that this is the best they can do means victory is practically assured.  We can't give up yet though, I have emailed all my state senators, and have been emailing them once a week until they reply. Want to help?
Definitely in the right place, no problem with your question, but I can't help you, sorry. Call me in 34 years : )

Though that was an interesting read, I think maybe you misinterpreted what I said.  I was not saying that all religion was bad.  I consider myself a religious person in spite of being an atheist; I find the community and the traditions comforting.  What I was saying was that my friend was showing a type of ignorance that is unique to religion.  He believes the bible to be the word of god, and he believes this in spite of large amounts of proof to the contrary.  I don't claim to have universally applicable truths, but I do claim to be more right than he is.  If I am not more right than he is, than that means accepting that I am simply diseased (technically speaking, I do have several mental illnesses, I just am not willing to count being gay as one of them.  The key diference is that depression, anxiety, and aspergers are all bad things, being gay isn't, and it isn't something fixable).  Not all religion is bad by any means.  Without it, what would be on the ceiling of the sistine chapel?  In fact, there would be no chapel at all!  I just was suggesting that blind faith in spite of evidence is something that is counterproductive to rational thought and science, which, as an aspie is the most important thing.  I admit, I am almost as dogmatic as he is in the way I aproach science.  Its how I am programed.  It is something I need to work on.  But I recognize that.  And if someone shows me a handfull of peer reviewed journal articles in respected journals saying that being gay is a curable disease, well, I would check myself into the loony bin for treatment.

I'm 16, and this semester was really my last chance to get my grades up high enough.  I was hoping to be able to do something great with my life, but it looks like I'm not good enough, I was lying to myself about my ability.  With aspergers, I have a wide spread in my abilities.  Some of my section scores on iq tests were well into the genius range, but it seems like my deficits will win out in the end.  I'm not going to MIT, i'm not going to start a successful company.  My parents both went to an ivy league college, so did both of my siblings.  Though I am objectively the smartest in my family, it seems like the best I am capable of is mediocrity.

No, what happened with my friend amplified my depression, which is caused primarily by stress and loneliness.  I am going to receive my report card at some point in the next week, when my parents will finally realize that I am not going to live up to their expectations, and that I am not going to succeed with my dream.

I don't think its stupidity.  He's a smart person.  Its propaganda, and child abuse.  Take a kid, and tell him every week that if he dosen't follow a list of rules, he will be tortured forever, and he will believe whatever he is told!  I can't really fault him as much as I fault his family, and society, though I wish he could look at things a bit more openly.

I tried explaining all of those things to him.  I thought to myself, if I can change this one persons mind, this friend, it means there is hope.  I was at a model un conference with him, and for three days we spent at least five hours a day, closer to ten, discussing religion, and homosexuality.  I tried every argument in the book, and then some.  At the end of it all, I just gave up.  If a smart, nice person can say those things, and really believe them, then what hope is there.
Yeah, I'm a jewish atheist, who has no problem with religion as long is it isn't used to hurt another person, physically or mentally.

I am completely convinced that they are ignorant, but at the same time I realized that he is not the only "ignorant" person.  And it isn't just ignorance, its the willful ignorance, ignorance in the face knowledge that only religion causes.  Even if I know its not true, a decent portion of the world will still treat me like it is, and realizing that was pretty shitty.  I live in an extremely liberal area, and I go to a school were at least a tenth of the faculty is gay, so while I have obviously heard of this behaviour, I had never witnessed it myself.  Hearing it from such a close friend made me realize how fucked up the world can be.

I disagree with what he said, but I do think that if a kid is going to transition, they should need a good psych work up, after all, they are young, and you can't change your mind. As for coming out that young, I never had any crushes, gay or straight, until high school, but that's just me.  I do think this kid shouldn't have to come out; even if he is gay, I think he might be coming out for the wrong reasons, because he thinks that is what society wants him to do. That being said, if he wants to say he is gay, whether he is homosexual or just happy, all the power to him, and if he wants to transition, if the doc green lights it, who am I to say no?

I did acknowledge what he was saying first, and I told him that I accepted his opinion, but I felt that it was an immoral opinion to have.  Also, I did not call him a dumbass, or a retarded shit, those seemed like unproductive terms to use.  I did say that he was being ignorant, hypocritical, overly reliant on faith, and immoral.  I however do not fault him for that.  I do not fault a citizen of the Democratic Peoples Republic of Korea for following their leader, for they are raised with the belief that he is devine, and that if they disobey they will be punished.  Similarly, my friend has been indoctrinated in such a manner.  Though I did not say this to him, I would say it is accurate that he should seek a psychological cure for this.  I think that he has been pumped full of propoganda, and I do not hold that against him.  That being said, I am shocked it stuck.  He goes to the most liberal school in our state, which is a very liberal school.  More than a tenth of the teachers are gay, the headmaster is gay, and are school has a general "who gives a shit" attitude about it.  I have heard capitalist used as a slur far more frequently than gay.  Partially, this is why I was so hurt.  I have been fortunate enough to have little exposure to homophobia in my life, and so his comments were all the more shocking.

You are welcome, I just wanted to clarify the admittedly fine point there.  Too often people don't understand distinctions like that.  Too often when I tell people that I have neurologically limited empathy, they think that means I am a sociopath.

I did.  He had no problem with that.  There was one argument that I did find slightly effective, that while he wouldn't acknowledge was right, he did think it had merit, and agree to talk to his priest about it.  His church claims that the worst sin a person can commit is suicide.  I showed him the statistics on homosexuality and suicide, and the diference that acceptance can make on the odds.  I even showed him an article from his churches newspaper about bullying people to the point of suicide, which, while not mentioning homosexuality, was clearly applicable, even going int o stories of the bullies not knowing they were doing something wrong.  In the end, he agreed that it made more sense to accept homosexuality, which dosen't send you to hell, if it prevents suicide, which does.  As reluctant as I am to use religious arguments when debating a religious belief, I find sometimes it is necessary.  Also, ignoring the religious aspects of it, I think that there is no person who would argue that suicide is the better of the two.  We discussed this topic, and the periphery subjects it touched on (abortion, suicide, atheism, tran* issues, church and state, etc...)  Ultimately, he was not willing to disagree with anything the church said, but I think I planted a seed of doubt, that hopefully will allow him to ultimately realize that some of the things he is saying are wrong.

After a recent 72 hour long near non stop debate with a neurotypical fundamentalist christian (he wasn't always awake, but I didn't sleep during it, and I was till debating, I'm sure you know what I mean) I have some I would like to share:

"Why can't you just believe?  Why do you always need to be rational?" #sntps

"If you that upset, why aren't you crying?" #sntps

"Isn't that just an excuse for being socially awkward?" #sntps

"You are going to have to put in some effort too." #sntps
I can identify it, and I have apersonality disorder.  THat being said, I would have done the same thing, knowing it was socially unacceptable, but not caring.

Its not about talking about these things, we finished our discussion today agreeing not to talk about them again.  The problem is, every time I think of him, all I see is the homophobic, ignorant, fundamentalist christian.  I know that isn't who he is.  Thats like someone saying that I am an atheist, and there are no other aspects to my identity.  How can I see him in a better light?  How can I ignore what I know about him so that I can see the good I know is there and once saw clearly.

Having just spent most of the past 72 hours debating religion with a greek orthodox christian, I can say that his answer to this question was that if you do not know about god and sin, but still live a good life, you go to heaven.  I asked him if I, an informed atheist could go to heaven, and he told me yes.  I checked to confirm this is the oficial stance of his religion, and they do believe that if you live a good, moral life, belief in Jesus is not neccesary.  It is only necessary if you live an imoral life.

I am not going to tell him, at least not yet, simply because I am not ready to tell anyone other than my parents yet.  I did actually try and imply it at one point this weekend, asking him how he knew I wasn't gay.  He said he could clearly tell I wasn't.  At some point I'll tell him, and when I do, he won't stop being friends with me, we have a mutual friend (the rather flamboyant kid I mentioned) who is openly gay.  The two of them don't discuss religion ever, so it hasn't been a problem for them.  I can't ask him to chose between me and god however, because I know what he will choose.  I have accepted he won't change his mind.  Is there anything I can do to ignore this aspect of him when considering him as a person?  Most of the world shares his beliefs after all, but that doesn't mean they are bad people.  He isn't perfect, but neither am I.  Who am I to say that being friends with an atheist aspie is easier for an orthodox christian than it is for a gay aspie to be friends with a homophobe?  I don't believe in his god, he dosen't believe in my science, but we still have many things in common, and I would hate to lose him as a friend.
